hints: Focus on what kind of reaction a Group 2 metal oxide has with water, is it redox to make hydrogen or just an acid-base reaction?
Remember that CaO, SrO and BaO all react readily with cold water to give only the hydroxide, with the general equation $\text{MO} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{M(OH)}_2$.
Check each statement for two things, does the oxide react under those conditions, and is hydrogen really a product or just the hydroxide plus water?
walkthrough:
**Recall the oxide plus water pattern**

Group 2 oxides are basic oxides. They simply add water to form the hydroxide only, no hydrogen is made.

Chemical equation rule:
$$\text{MO(s)} + \text{H}_2\text{O(l)} \rightarrow \text{M(OH)}_2\text{(aq)}$$

**Recall the trend down Group 2**

Reactivity with water increases down the group. $\text{CaO}$, $\text{SrO}$ and $\text{BaO}$ all react vigorously at room temperature, while $\text{MgO}$ reacts only very slowly with cold water.

So any statement saying calcium oxide does not react is already suspicious.

**Apply to each statement and conclude**

Barium oxide should give only $\text{Ba(OH)}_2$, not hydrogen. Calcium oxide does react, this is slaking of lime. Magnesium hydroxide on heating decomposes to $\text{MgO} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$, not hydrogen.

That leaves only the strontium oxide statement which fits the pattern perfectly:
$$\text{SrO(s)} + \text{H}_2\text{O(l)} \rightarrow \text{Sr(OH)}_2\text{(aq)}$$

options.A: Incorrect. $\text{BaO} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{Ba(OH)}_2$ only. No hydrogen is formed because this is not a redox reaction. Students often confuse this with barium metal + water, which does give hydrogen.
options.B: Incorrect. Calcium oxide does react readily with cold water to form calcium hydroxide, $\text{CaO} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{Ca(OH)}_2$. This is the well known slaking reaction and it is exothermic.
options.C: Incorrect. Magnesium hydroxide does not react with steam to give hydrogen. On strong heating it decomposes to $\text{Mg(OH)}_2 \rightarrow \text{MgO} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$. Hydrogen comes from magnesium metal + steam, not from the hydroxide.
options.D: Correct. Strontium oxide is a basic Group 2 oxide and reacts readily with water at room temperature to give strontium hydroxide only: $\text{SrO} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{Sr(OH)}_2$. No other product is formed.
